# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 44 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 44 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_044_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 1 — Drive Out Evil Desire

**44:1** He said to me: "Strip out every evil desire from yourself and clothe yourself in good and holy desire instead. Because when you do that — when you're clothed in good desire — you'll find you can hate evil desire and keep it under control. Evil desire is a wild beast; it's extremely difficult to tame. It's terrifying, and it devours people with its savagery. God's servants especially get consumed by it when they don't know how to deal with it."

**44:2** "What exactly does evil desire do to destroy God's servants?" I asked. "List them for me so I know what to avoid." "Listen," he said. "Here are the ways evil desire kills those who serve God."

**44:3** "The worst is lusting after someone else's spouse. Then comes the craving for excessive wealth, the appetite for unnecessary amounts of food and drink, and the hunger for various other foolish indulgences. Every kind of luxury is foolish and worthless for God's servants. These desires are evil — they lead to death for God's servants. Evil desire is a child of the devil himself. So you have to stay away from evil desires. Staying away from them is how you truly live for God."

**44:4** "Those who are controlled by these desires and refuse to resist them will be completely destroyed — these desires lead to death, plain and simple. But you — if you pursue righteousness and goodness — clothe yourself in the desire for those things. Renounce every evil desire, put on desire that is good and honorable and pleasing to God, and you will live for God. Everyone who lives this way will."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the urgent ethical tone of Hermas's teaching on desire.*
